workflowDefinition.name: Attack Discovery
workflowDefinition.description: Watch Floor Attack Discovery worker. Owns the schedule and dispatches to the global Attack Discovery worker, which runs generation and fans out one review per generated attack.

yaml:
version: "1"
name: Attack Discovery
description: >
  Watch Floor Attack Discovery worker. Owns the schedule and dispatches to the
  global Attack Discovery worker, which runs generation and fans out one review
  per generated attack.
enabled: true
tags:
  - watch
  - watch-floor
settings:
  run_as: "kibana/az-worker-sa"
  # This worker is installed per space, so the key needs no space component.
  #
  # `cancel-in-progress` with max 1: the newest discoveries are the ones worth
  # having, and a backlog must never delay a new scheduled run. Neither alternative
  # delivers that — `drop` turns the newer run away, and `queue` makes it wait behind
  # superseded work (a QUEUED run does not hold the slot, but it does not pass the run
  # ahead of it either, and `queue-ttl` expires it after 24h). The global runner this
  # worker dispatches to sets the same policy.
  #
  # Cancelling is only safe because a run of this worker is bounded by generation. It
  # holds its slot for as long as the runner it waits on, and the runner dispatches
  # the per-attack reviews detached rather than waiting on their escalation gates. If
  # that ever changed, this schedule would cancel a previous run's parked gates —
  # every 24h by default, and as often as every minute if an operator sets the
  # interval that low.
  #
  # Must be an object — unlike a `parallel` step's `concurrency`, workflow-level
  # `settings.concurrency` does not accept a bare number.
  concurrency:
    key: floor-attack-discovery
    strategy: cancel-in-progress
    max: 1
triggers:
  - type: scheduled
    with:
      every: "24h"
consts:
  worker_settings:
    settingsVersion: 1
    autonomy: "manual"
    scheduleInterval: "24h"
steps:
  # Synchronous on purpose: #19276 requires that when generation fails after its
  # built-in retries, this worker run remains failed and hands off nothing.
  # `workflow.execute` propagates the child's failure, which `workflow.executeAsync`
  # would not — the run would report success while generation had failed. The cost
  # is that this worker waits for the child to finish before it continues, and keeps
  # its single concurrency slot for that whole time. That cost stays bounded because
  # the child returns once generation has run and the reviews are dispatched, not
  # once they are decided.
  #
  # The child carries no schedule of its own; this worker is the single scheduler
  # authority for the space.
  - name: run_attack_discovery
    type: workflow.execute
    with:
      workflow-id: system-security-attack-discovery-worker
      # Runs the global runner, and every child it starts, as this worker's service
      # account. Requires `run_as`; the worker cannot be enabled without one.
      run-as-mode: inherit
      inputs:
        # All three worker settings are forwarded. `autonomy` decides how the child's
        # review handles a true-positive verdict; the other two are traceability only
        # and are echoed in the child's output.
        # `${{ }}` preserves the value's type so the editor does not type-check the
        # template source against the child's enum / maxLength constraints.
        autonomy: "${{ consts.worker_settings.autonomy }}"
        settings_version: "${{ consts.worker_settings.settingsVersion }}"
        schedule_interval: "${{ consts.worker_settings.scheduleInterval }}"
        parent_run_id: "{{ execution.id }}"
